---
title: "Effect of local resolution weighting"
format:
  html:
    embed-resources: true
jupyter: python3
---

Single-pass composites against the local resolution-weighted (LRW) GLACE composite in
steep terrain: the ascending-only and descending-only unweighted mean composites, the
LRW composite and its composite quality map (QA-CQM), for one 10 km window. A switch
selects VV backscatter or VV coherence; the CQM is the one written with that layer.
Pixels a single-pass composite has no valid observation for (radar shadow, in
backscatter) are drawn in a non-white colour. The CQM is the reciprocal of the
composite's effective local scattering area, drawn in dB as in Small et al. (2022):
higher is better resolved. 0 dB is a facet at 45° local incidence; flat terrain is
about −1 dB, the tangent of the incidence angle.

The LRW composite and its CQM are the GLACE tiles of the Alps-wide run
(`config/lrw-alps.yml`, `alps-total/{year}/s1-comp`, byte-identical to the
published ones). The pass composites are not part of GLACE: they come from
`config/pass-alps.yml`, run over the glaciers of the Alps on the same burst
products and written to `alps-total/{year}/s1-comp-pass`. Both share the compositing
window, the 35x7 coherence window and the mean. The tiles under the window are
mosaicked on reading, so it may span several of them.

```{python}
import cmcrameri.cm as cmc
from matplotlib.font_manager import FontProperties
from matplotlib.patches import Patch
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
from matplotlib_inline.backend_inline import set_matplotlib_formats
import numpy as np
from pyproj import CRS, Transformer

from glace_production.config import settings
from glace_production.plotting import add_scalebar, set_context, set_style
from data_paths import PASS_CONFIG, run_dirs
from regions import LRW_REGION, REGION_EPSG, region_bounds
from tiles import read_window, tile_file, window_tiles

set_style()
set_context("paper")
set_matplotlib_formats("retina")
```

## Configuration

The window is `LRW_REGION` in `regions.py` beside this notebook, selected like the
mapping examples' by its lower-left corner (UTM 32N, metres, on the 10 m grid), and 10
km on a side; the dataset overview marks it with them. Gurgler Ferner (Austrian
Glacier Inventory GI5) flows north into the north-south Gurgler Tal, so the ascending
(east-looking) and descending (west-looking) passes see each valley side at a fine
resolution in one pass and foreshortened in the other.

```{python}
LAYER = "coh"  # "coh" for VV coherence (the paper figure), "rtc" for VV backscatter
REGION = LRW_REGION

FIGURE_NAME = "lrw-effect"  # saved as {FIGURE_NAME}-{LAYER}.pdf in FIGURE_DIR
FIGURE_DIR = settings.figures_dir / FIGURE_NAME  # one folder per notebook
FIGURE_DIR.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)

# One stretch for the three composites, rounded from their pooled percentiles, which
# are printed to compare against. The CQM is drawn as 10 log10(CQM), as in Small et al.
# (2022); 0 dB is a facet at 45° local incidence, flat terrain about -1 dB.
STRETCH_PERCENTILES = (2, 98)
LAYERS = {
    "rtc": {
        "prefix": "S1_RTC",
        "label": "VV backscatter (dB)",
        "cmap": cmc.navia,
        "vmin": -20,
        "vmax": 0,
        "ticks": np.arange(-20, 0 + 1e-6, 5),
    },
    "coh": {
        "prefix": "S1_COH12",
        "label": "VV coherence",
        "cmap": cmc.lipari,
        "vmin": 0.0,
        "vmax": 0.8,
        "ticks": np.arange(0.0, 0.8 + 1e-6, 0.2),
    },
}
CQM_CMAP = cmc.oslo
CQM_VMIN, CQM_VMAX = -6, 6
CQM_TICKS = np.arange(CQM_VMIN, CQM_VMAX + 1e-6, 3)
CQM_LABEL = "Composite quality (dB)"
# Pixels without a valid observation: radar shadow in a single-pass composite. A violet
# magenta, which stays apart from navia, lipari and oslo under deuteranopia, protanopia
# and tritanopia as well (a grey or a darker magenta falls onto navia's blues)
NODATA_COLOR = "#c000ff"
NODATA_LABEL = "No valid observation"

# Hung from one top line, so a title may break over two lines; the colormaps tell the
# composites (a-c) from the quality map (d), and the titles pair c with d
TITLES = ["Ascending", "Descending", "GLACE", "GLACE composite\nquality map"]

# Layout in mm: four square panels in one row fill the width, and the figure height
# follows from them; Nature's maximum is 180 mm x 215 mm. The composites' colorbar is
# centred below b and reaches into a and c, so it reads as theirs; the CQM's sits below d.
MM = 1 / 25.4  # inches per mm
FIG_WIDTH = 180
GAP = 2.0  # between the panels
MARGIN_LEFT = 0.5
MARGIN_RIGHT = 0.5
TITLE_TOP = 0.5  # from the figure's top edge to the top of the titles
MARGIN_TOP = 8.4  # panel titles, up to two lines, and 1.2 mm
COLORBAR_GAP = 2.0  # between the maps and the colorbars
# Colorbars and scalebars as in mapping-examples.qmd, relative to the panel width: the
# extend triangles (5 % of the bar each) stay inside the panel
COLORBAR_WIDTH = 0.90  # fraction of the panel width, centred below it
COLORBAR_ASPECT = 20  # colorbar length over thickness, as matplotlib's `aspect`
COLORBAR_EXTENDFRAC = 0.05  # matplotlib's default, of the one-panel CQM bar
# The composites' bar, in panel widths; its thickness and triangles are the CQM bar's
LAYER_COLORBAR_WIDTH = 1.5
MARGIN_BOTTOM = 11.0  # below the colorbars' top edge: their ticks, label and 0.5 mm
SCALEBAR_FONTSIZE = 7  # pt, one step below the body text: an annotation on the map
```

```{python}
MAP_CRS = CRS.from_epsg(REGION_EPSG)
layer = LAYERS[LAYER]
year = REGION["year"]
bounds = region_bounds(REGION)

LRW_DIR = run_dirs(year).comp_dir
PASS_DIR = run_dirs(year, PASS_CONFIG).comp_dir

# The tiles in the window's UTM zone that overlap it; one that only touches its edge is
# left out
tiles = window_tiles(bounds, REGION_EPSG)
print(f"tiles: {', '.join(tiles)}")

prefix = layer["prefix"]
patterns = {
    "asc": (PASS_DIR, f"{prefix}_COMP_A_{{tile}}_VV_*.tif"),
    "dsc": (PASS_DIR, f"{prefix}_COMP_D_{{tile}}_VV_*.tif"),
    "lrw": (LRW_DIR, f"{prefix}_LRW_{{tile}}_VV_*.tif"),
    "cqm": (LRW_DIR, f"{prefix}_LRW_QA-CQM_{{tile}}_VV_*.tif"),
}
data = {
    key: read_window([tile_file(d, pattern, t) for t in tiles], bounds, REGION_EPSG)
    for key, (d, pattern) in patterns.items()
}
if LAYER == "rtc":  # every composite is linear; drawn in dB
    for key in ("asc", "dsc", "lrw"):
        with np.errstate(divide="ignore", invalid="ignore"):
            data[key] = np.where(data[key] > 0, 10 * np.log10(data[key]), np.nan)
with np.errstate(divide="ignore", invalid="ignore"):  # the CQM is linear; drawn in dB
    data["cqm"] = np.where(data["cqm"] > 0, 10 * np.log10(data["cqm"]), np.nan)
```

The share of the window without a valid observation in each composite, and the
stretch percentiles:

```{python}
for key in ("asc", "dsc", "lrw", "cqm"):
    print(f"{key}: {np.mean(~np.isfinite(data[key])):.1%} without a valid observation")
both = ~np.isfinite(data["asc"]) & ~np.isfinite(data["dsc"])
print(f"missing in both passes: {both.mean():.2%}")

pooled = np.concatenate([data[k][np.isfinite(data[k])] for k in ("asc", "dsc", "lrw")])
lo, hi = np.percentile(pooled, STRETCH_PERCENTILES)
print(f"{STRETCH_PERCENTILES} % {layer['label']}: {lo:.2f} to {hi:.2f}")
print(f"stretch: {layer['vmin']} to {layer['vmax']}")
cqm = data["cqm"][np.isfinite(data["cqm"])]
print(f"{STRETCH_PERCENTILES} % CQM: {np.percentile(cqm, STRETCH_PERCENTILES).round(1)} dB")
print(f"CQM < 0 dB: {np.mean(cqm < 0):.1%}, stretch: {CQM_VMIN} to {CQM_VMAX} dB")
```

Window centre for the caption, in WGS 84:

```{python}
left, bottom, right, top = bounds
lon, lat = Transformer.from_crs(MAP_CRS, "EPSG:4326", always_xy=True).transform(
    (left + right) / 2, (bottom + top) / 2
)
print(f"{REGION['name']}, {year}: {lat:.4f}° N, {lon:.4f}° E")
```

## Figure

```{python}
def with_bad(cmap):
    """``cmap`` with NaN drawn in ``NODATA_COLOR``."""
    cmap = cmap.copy()
    cmap.set_bad(NODATA_COLOR)
    return cmap


def extend(values: list[np.ndarray], vmin: float, vmax: float) -> str:
    """Colorbar ``extend`` for the ends of ``[vmin, vmax]`` the finite values exceed."""
    low = any(np.nanmin(v) < vmin for v in values)
    high = any(np.nanmax(v) > vmax for v in values)
    return {(False, False): "neither", (True, False): "min", (False, True): "max"}.get(
        (low, high), "both"
    )


# Every position in mm from the top-left corner. Titles and colorbar ticks must fit
# the margins: nothing moves the panels to make room.
panel_mm = (FIG_WIDTH - MARGIN_LEFT - MARGIN_RIGHT - 3 * GAP) / 4
column_xs = [MARGIN_LEFT + j * (panel_mm + GAP) for j in range(4)]
cbar_y = MARGIN_TOP + panel_mm + COLORBAR_GAP
fig_height = cbar_y + MARGIN_BOTTOM
print(f"figure {FIG_WIDTH} mm x {fig_height:.1f} mm, panels {panel_mm:.2f} mm")


def rect(x: float, y: float, width: float, height: float) -> tuple[float, float, float, float]:
    """Figure-fraction rectangle of a box at (x, y) mm from the top-left corner."""
    return (x / FIG_WIDTH, 1 - (y + height) / fig_height, width / FIG_WIDTH, height / fig_height)


def draw_title(x: float, letter: str, title: str) -> None:
    """Bold panel ``letter`` at ``x`` mm and bold ``title`` centred on the panel there,
    both hung from TITLE_TOP."""
    kwargs = {
        "fontsize": plt.rcParams["axes.titlesize"],
        "fontweight": "bold",
        "va": "top",
    }
    y = 1 - TITLE_TOP / fig_height
    fig.text(x / FIG_WIDTH, y, letter, ha="left", **kwargs)
    fig.text(
        (x + panel_mm / 2) / FIG_WIDTH, y, title, ha="center", multialignment="center", **kwargs
    )


fig = plt.figure(figsize=(FIG_WIDTH * MM, fig_height * MM))
axs = [fig.add_axes(rect(x, MARGIN_TOP, panel_mm, panel_mm)) for x in column_xs]
kwargs = {"extent": (left, right, bottom, top), "origin": "upper", "interpolation": "nearest"}
cmap = with_bad(layer["cmap"])
for ax, key in zip(axs[:3], ("asc", "dsc", "lrw"), strict=True):
    im = ax.imshow(data[key], cmap=cmap, vmin=layer["vmin"], vmax=layer["vmax"], **kwargs)
cqm_im = axs[3].imshow(
    data["cqm"], cmap=with_bad(CQM_CMAP), vmin=CQM_VMIN, vmax=CQM_VMAX, **kwargs
)
for ax, x, letter, title in zip(axs, column_xs, "abcd", TITLES, strict=True):
    ax.set(xticks=[], yticks=[])
    ax.spines[:].set_visible(False)
    draw_title(x, letter, title)

add_scalebar(
    axs[3],
    style="filled",
    loc="lower right",
    crs=MAP_CRS,
    linewidth=plt.rcParams["axes.linewidth"],
    prop=FontProperties(size=SCALEBAR_FONTSIZE),
)

# The composites' colorbar centred under b, reaching into a and c, the CQM's under d.
# Both share the CQM bar's thickness and the length of its extend triangles, so the
# longer bar takes a proportionally smaller extendfrac.
cbar_width = COLORBAR_WIDTH * panel_mm
cbar_height = cbar_width / COLORBAR_ASPECT
layer_width = LAYER_COLORBAR_WIDTH * panel_mm
layer_cax = fig.add_axes(
    rect(column_xs[1] + (panel_mm - layer_width) / 2, cbar_y, layer_width, cbar_height)
)
cqm_cax = fig.add_axes(
    rect(column_xs[3] + (panel_mm - cbar_width) / 2, cbar_y, cbar_width, cbar_height)
)
fig.colorbar(
    im,
    cax=layer_cax,
    orientation="horizontal",
    extend=extend([data[k] for k in ("asc", "dsc", "lrw")], layer["vmin"], layer["vmax"]),
    extendfrac=COLORBAR_EXTENDFRAC * cbar_width / layer_width,
    label=layer["label"],
    ticks=layer["ticks"],
)
fig.colorbar(
    cqm_im,
    cax=cqm_cax,
    orientation="horizontal",
    extend=extend([data["cqm"]], CQM_VMIN, CQM_VMAX),
    extendfrac=COLORBAR_EXTENDFRAC,
    label=CQM_LABEL,
    ticks=CQM_TICKS,
)
# The no-data patch below panel a, where a composite has pixels without an observation
if any(np.isnan(data[k]).any() for k in ("asc", "dsc", "lrw", "cqm")):
    fig.legend(
        handles=[Patch(facecolor=NODATA_COLOR, edgecolor="none", label=NODATA_LABEL)],
        loc="upper left",
        bbox_to_anchor=(column_xs[0] / FIG_WIDTH, 1 - cbar_y / fig_height),
        borderaxespad=0,
        borderpad=0,
        handletextpad=0.5,
    )
with (FIGURE_DIR / f"{FIGURE_NAME}-{LAYER}.pdf").open("wb") as f:
    fig.savefig(f, format="pdf", bbox_inches=None)
```
